example.com
H1Lily's photography page

A main content heading

  • The outline is read by tags, not by font size
  • Heading levels show nesting; unnecessary skips can make the outline harder to follow

Biggest font size does not mean highest level: heading tags express structure, visual size is only styling.

Why heading levels have an order

Use H1 according to the content: HTML allows multiple H1s; check whether each marks a distinct main section instead of deleting one just because of the count.

Levels descend in order: H1→H2→H3 can express nested sections; skipping a level unnecessarily can make the outline harder to follow, but is not an HTML syntax error by itself.

Machines and people read it: Screen readers can navigate by headings; font size only affects appearance and cannot replace heading structure.

What people often confuse

Biggest font size does not mean highest level: heading tags express structure, visual size is styling. Multiple H1s are allowed; the headings should still organize the page clearly.
